correctness.rationale: From the exact two-dimensional multiplication and alpha,beta of Example 1 over any field K with a !=0, direct simultaneous commutation forces R=[[r,b(r-t)/a],[0,t]] and S=[[s,b(s-v)/a],[0,v]]. Evaluate both Rota–Baxter system equations on all four ordered basis pairs; the defining ideal has field-valued zero locus rs=0, tv=0, t(r-s-t)=0, (a-1)v(r-s+v)=0. Independent symbolic SymPy reconstruction verified the basis defects and the remaining independent scalar constraints rather than trusting VERIFY_OK. If a!=1, case-splitting t,v gives six lines meeting at origin; when a=1 the v equation drops, giving two planes meeting in v-axis plus two additional lines meeting at origin. Inclusion-exclusion gives 6q-5 and 2q^2+q-2; extension fields replace q by q^m, producing displayed reduced zeta functions. Checked finite rational examples plus the original four prime-field enumerations as secondary evidence; equality of polynomial conditions is the all-field proof.

value.rationale: A natural finite-dimensional algebra example has a nontrivial moduli-space stratification: six lines jump to two planes and lines at a=1, with exact point counts and zeta functions. This is a complete classification of all compatible operator pairs, not a routine single substituted example, and is independently useful as a singular/degenerate test case for BiHom Rota–Baxter theory.
